name: Carina Dwarf
tagline: A Milky Way satellite 330,000 light-years out whose star-formation history comes in separate bursts across cosmic time.
history: Carina is famous among dwarf spheroidals for a star-formation history written in separated pulses — an ancient burst, a middle-aged burst and a late one — rather than one epoch of star-making. That staircase of populations let astronomers read its accretion history: likely a slow early orbit around the Milky Way. Its stars are old and metal-poor, and deep surveys trace its light for thousands of light-years across the halo.
